mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 2% for 3 consecutive months predicts higher expected corporate financing costs, which reduces equity discount rates and drives positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses and stays above 2% for 3 months
regime_hint: tightening phase of the US interest rate cycle
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative or flat despite the FEDFUNDS condition, or discount rate sensitivity to FEDFUNDS is statistically insignificant (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly PAYEMS accompanied by a decline in UNRATE over the next month signals strengthening labor market conditions, which elevates consumer confidence and supports positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE decreases in the following month
regime_hint: early recovery in labor market after a soft landing
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative, or the combined labor indicators fail to predict returns with a Sharpe ratio >0.5 over 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly increase in HOUST (residential construction) followed by a positive GDP momentum (indirectly reflected via INDPRO) predicts rising future demand for consumer and business equities, yielding positive S&P 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >10% in a month and INDPRO rises in the next month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative despite the signal, or the correlation between the signal and returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in INDPRO for 2 consecutive months indicates weakening supply-side constraints, which reduces the risk of deflation and supports positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in >40% of INDPRO decline episodes, or the effect is not robust across multiple macro regimes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in CPIAUCSL below 105 (annualized) followed by a sustained rise in FEDFUNDS suggests conflicting inflation and policy signals, which can produce negative S&P 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL drops below 105 and FEDFUNDS rises over the next month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not statistically different from baseline during such episodes (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 6% for 4 consecutive months, it reflects increased labor market participation and wage growth, which tends to boost equity valuations and drive positive S&P 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 6% for 4 consecutive months
regime_hint: low unemployment and strong labor market
failure_condition: 60-day returns are flat or negative during such UNRATE declines, or the effect is not significant in a two-sample test.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in both PAYEMS and RSAFS for two months suggests robust business and consumer demand, which elevates earnings expectations and supports positive S&P 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and RSAFS both increase by >5% in the same month and persist for two months
failure_condition: 20-day returns fail to outperform a baseline model with only one demand proxy (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in GDPC1 (GDP) followed by a rebound in INDPRO within 10 days indicates a turning point from contraction to expansion, which often precedes positive S&P 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for 2 months then rises while INDPRO increases in the following trading day
regime_hint: turning from recession to growth in quarterly data
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not positive when the pattern is detected (or the pattern is not statistically significant).
